'''''Cystopteris fragilis''''' is a species of [[perennial]] [[fern]] known by the common names '''brittle bladder-fern'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref> and '''common fragile fern'''. It can be found worldwide, generally in shady, moist areas.

== Description ==
It has a short, black rootstock. The leaves are up to {{cvt|5-25|cm}} and are borne on fleshy [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]] with few or no long hairs. The petioles are about half the length of the leaf blade. Each leaf is divided into many pairs of leaflets, each of which is subdivided into lobed segments. The leaflets are narrowly triangular and [[Glossary of leaf morphology|apiculate]]. The underside of the leaf has many rounded [[sorus|sori]] containing the [[sporangium|sporangia]]. A young ''Cystopteris fragilis'' is said to have the scent of [[bitter almond]], which is caused by spores that  contain [[hydrogen cyanide]].<ref name="Piirainen">{{cite book |last1=Piirainen |first1=Mikko |title=Kotimaan luonnonkasvit |last2=Piirainen |first2=Pirkko |last3=Vainio |first3=Hannele |date=1999 |publisher=WSOY |isbn=951-0-23001-4 |location=Porvoo, Finland |page=36 |language=fi |trans-title=Native wild plants}}</ref>

== Habitat ==
The plant, native to for example Finland, grows in places fit for its brittle structure: usually shady and slightly moist areas, in the cracks and ledges of vertical rock faces, blockfields and sometimes on even cliff surfaces as well. It avoids the more most acidic and barren cliffs and prefers especially slightly lime rich soil.<ref name="Piirainen" />
